answer: In PoA, identity verification requires a Wesolowski VDF built from continuous sequential modular squarings: each result is the input to the next, so one identity’s proof has a strict physical delay. An attacker simulating many clones cannot compress that dependency chain or parallelize its steps across GPUs; each clone still consumes sequential time and hardware. Thus timber, marble, and canyon identities gain no shortcut, making Sybil expansion costly and detectable.
